title: Label a run for Revit's Undo history and revert or restore it with the undo and redo tools
task: Try a change, look at it, and take it back without touching the person's own work: pass execute_script label so the run appears in Revit's Undo history as 'MCP: <label>', then call the undo tool with confirm: true (redo to restore). The tool reports what it reverted: undo-reverted-connector-work names the labelled run; undo-reverted-other-work means a person's action was undone instead.

pitfalls.cause: Undo acts on Revit's global stack; the most recent action may be a person's.
pitfalls.fix: Ask the user, then call undo with confirm: true; the response says how long ago the connector last ran here.

pitfalls.cause: Someone acted in Revit after the labelled run, so their step was reverted instead.
pitfalls.fix: Call redo immediately to restore it, tell the user, and do not retry blindly.

pitfalls.symptom: Undo removes more than the one element the script created.
pitfalls.cause: All blocks of one run are one undo step; a run that made several blocks is reverted whole.
pitfalls.fix: Expected; split independent tasks into separate runs if they must be undoable separately.

pitfalls.symptom: undo-wrong-active-document, or the undo reverted a different document's step.
pitfalls.cause: The stack is per document and the tools act on the active document.
pitfalls.fix: Pass document_id of the document you expect to be active; route labelled runs at the active document.
